cases.title: FAA nationwide ground stop
cases.summary: The FAA temporarily stopped departures nationwide after instability in air traffic control telecommunications and radar data. The ground stop ended that evening; operational recovery continued into November 14.
cases.editorialNote: Historical, manually reviewed public-source snapshot. Not a live FAA status feed, flight manifest, current travel advisory, or definitive root-cause report.

sources.title: November 14: Airspace restoration and preliminary investigation

timeline.label: Communications and radar data instability
timeline.detail: In a November 13 briefing, the Transportation Secretary said inconsistencies at ATC centers and TRACONs began around 3:36 p.m. Eastern.

timeline.displayAt: Nov 13 · time not published in cited briefing
timeline.label: Nationwide departure ground stop
timeline.detail: The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop as a precaution while communications and radar stability was in question. No exact initiation minute is assigned here.

timeline.label: Airspace reopened
timeline.detail: Transportation Secretary Duffy reported that the airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern; departures were expected to resume gradually as crews and aircraft became available.

timeline.label: Operational recovery reported
timeline.detail: DOT said U.S. airspace was open again but passengers should anticipate delays and cancellations during the recovery.

timeline.label: Possible equipment or installation fault under investigation
timeline.detail: DOT described maintenance involving copper-to-fiber / TDM-to-IP migration and reported abnormal router connection attempts. Officials explicitly said the specific fault had not been determined. This is a preliminary account, not a settled root cause.
